prompts: After seven days, independently explain: Locate each of Liberia's 15 counties on an outline map and name its capital.

scenes.title: Read a schematic county map
scenes.learnerAction: Use the model, complete its task, and explain what the representation shows.

content.body: Explore the names and capital labels on this schematic. It is not a survey map: do not infer exact boundaries, distance, area or population from the shapes. The county and capital list is a repository reference awaiting independent authoritative-source attestation.

accessibility.textAlternative: Explore the names and capital labels on this schematic. It is not a survey map: do not infer exact boundaries, distance, area or population from the shapes. The county and capital list is a repository reference awaiting independent authoritative-source attestation. A schematic map of Liberia's 15 counties: Lofa (capital Voinjama), Gbarpolu (capital Bopolu), Grand Cape Mount (capital Robertsport), Bomi (capital Tubmanburg), Montserrado (capital Bensonville), Bong (capital Gbarnga), Nimba (capital Sanniquellie), Margibi (capital Kakata), Grand Bassa (capital Buchanan), River Cess (capital Cestos City), Grand Gedeh (capital Zwedru), Sinoe (capital Greenville), River Gee (capital Fish Town), Grand Kru (capital Barclayville), Maryland (capital Harper).

scenes.title: Compare evidence independently
scenes.learnerAction: Compare the capital and county names in the two entries. Explain how the labels keep them distinct. Can a larger drawn county establish a larger population? Explain what additional source would be needed.

content.body: The repository model lists Bong: Gbarnga; Montserrado: Bensonville. Treat the schematic as a name-location aid, not a measurement of land or people.

content.body: Worked reasoning: a county-capital table supports a claim about administrative names. It does not establish travel time or population. A useful explanation states both what a source supports and what remains unknown.

accessibility.textAlternative: Worked reasoning: a county-capital table supports a claim about administrative names. It does not establish travel time or population. blocks.question: Which statements justify checking a county-capital claim with a named source?

sentences.text: The map labels each county and its capital separately.
sentences.why: The two labels distinguish the administrative units.

sentences.text: The schematic does not encode population or reliable distances.
sentences.why: A source has limits; use a population table or a scaled map for other claims.

sentences.text: A familiar-looking shape is enough to verify every administrative fact.
sentences.why: Visual familiarity is not verification against an authoritative list.
